result.title: Selective Transfer through Sequence Distillation: From Benchmark Knowledge to Backdoor Behaviour
result.summary: Knowledge distillation is widely used to transfer capabilities from teacher models to student models, but recent work shows that it can also transfer unintended teacher properties. We study whether different hidden teacher properties survive the same distillation channels. Specifically, we compare two properties: benchmark-associated knowledge and refusal backdoors, and show that distillation treats them very differently. Teachers fine-tuned on benchmark data successfully pass that knowledge to students through all four distillation channels we test, including when students are trained only on teacher-generated number sequences containing no natural language or domain content whatsoever. Refusal backdoors tell the opposite story: backdoored teachers achieve near-perfect triggered refusal, yet sequence-distilled students inherit essentially none of this behaviour. Logit-based distillation transfers it substantially, reaching up to 85.5\% triggered refusal in students that saw zero backdoor examples. Distillation is therefore selective, and the selection criterion is not what data the student sees, but what structure the teacher's property has. The code is available at https://github.com/MJonibek/kd-leakage.

AI.brief_summary: 论文比较基准知识与拒绝后门两类隐藏教师属性在同四种知识蒸馏通道中的传递差异：基准知识可通过全部通道（含纯数字序列）传递，而后门几乎无法经序列表蒸馏继承，需靠 logit 蒸馏才能达到最高 85.5% 的触发拒绝率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其结果提示监督信号所在的层级（离散输出序列 vs 分布/logit）决定了隐藏行为能否传递，这可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练与 latent 状态监督该挂在哪一层提供可核查的方法线索。
